To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people who are motivated to derogate an innocent victim will use relative judgments (i.e., compare the victim to others) to do so, but they will use absolute judgments to derogate a guilty victim.

the use of absolute compared with relative measures of an innocent victims’ character enables observers to avoid derogating the victim without transparent violations of social norms and values proscribing derogations.
people are more likely to derogate innocent victims when they are asked to evaluate them relative to others than when they are asked about their character on an absolute scale.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which social norms are used to justify the suppression and derogation of prejudice.
how people can derogate innocent victims without appearing to be derogating innocent victims.
the psychological processes by which observers justify derogating victims of prejudice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of absolute versus relative scales in the measurement of innocent victim characteristics may affect the extent to which the innocent victim is derogated.
relative measures of innocent victims’ characters are more derogated than absolute measures, which is a result of the ambiguity of the relative measures.
relative measures allow observers to derogate victims in ways that are more transparent than absolute measures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
relative judgments allow people to derogate innocent victims without violating social norms proscribing derogation of innocent victims.
the use of comparative judgments enables individuals to derogate innocent victims without violating social norms proscribing derogation.

the use of a relative versus absolute measure of an innocent victim's character enables observers to express their negative attitudes towards the victim while maintaining their self-image of being a good person.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of absolute and relative judgments can have different consequences for evaluations of the innocent victim.
the social comparison of innocent victims to the average person can be used to derogate them without appearing prejudiced.
the social comparison processes used to evaluate victims may be more complex than they first appear.
